video.title: He Made $60K His First Month With This Boring Business

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Mike from Iowa City, a tile installer who launched a garage-floor concrete coatings business (flake floors using polyurea base and polyaspartic top coat) around February-March 2026 with his brother and two experienced partners. He claims $60K revenue in April and $69K in May with over 50% profit, driven almost entirely by Meta ads, instant phone follow-up, upfront $8/sq ft pricing and a 10% deposit. Key takeaways: blue-collar service bars are low (answer the phone, show up, be transparent on price), AI (Claude) writes all ad copy and advises on ad budgets, and startup cost can be roughly $15-25K or under $1K by renting a grinder.

speakers.name: Mike
speakers.description: Tile contractor from Iowa City who runs Old Cap Coatings (concrete coatings) with partners; one of four partners

ideas.name: Garage floor flake coatings (Old Cap Coatings)
ideas.one_liner: Grind, coat and flake residential garage floors with polyurea base and polyaspartic top coat at $8/sq ft, one-day jobs, sold via Meta lead ads.
ideas.business_model: Per-job price per square foot with 10% non-refundable deposit; balance paid after the job.
ideas.customer: Mostly homeowners aged 50+, typically male, with 2-4 car garages; also some interior, patio, pool deck and commercial (a church, a warehouse).
ideas.problem: Bare or pitted concrete garage floors look bad and stain; owners want a decorative, easy-clean, durable finish.
ideas.offer: Decorative flake garage floor (grind, polyurea base coat, broadcast flake, polyaspartic top coat) installed in one day by a two-person crew, with optional move-your-stuff add-on.

pricing.model: Flat $8 per sq ft for everything, published in ads; add-ons for steps and stem walls

price_points.label: Optional extra to have contents moved

pricing.notes: Premium vs competitors; one competitor about 50% cheaper. Little discounting; 10% off offered for winter interior bookings. Credit card accepted, no financing.

acquisition_channels.details: Meta (mostly Facebook, targeted 55+ males) lead-form ads showing grinding and flake-throwing video (~23 seconds); 80-90%+ of leads. Best ad hook is brother asking 'how much does it cost?' with price stated. Added one qualifying question (interior/garage/exterior/other). Spend about $200/day, doubled to $400/day for second crew; 50-mile radius.

quote.text: it's all basically all meta ads. Yeah. We get some Google traffic. We have a referral program, but it's mostly meta.
quote.speaker: Mike

acquisition_channels.details: Google Local Services Ads used alongside; modest traffic. Not on Thumbtack or Angi.
First three jobs came from friends/church at early-bird discount; $200 referral program produced a ~$30K warehouse job; happy customers recommend contractors.

quote.text: That $200 referral turned into like a $30,000 job cuz we got his mom to do it.
quote.speaker: Mike

acquisition_channels.details: Ask for reviews so the Google Business Profile ranks naturally.

ideas.delivery: Two-person crew (lead at about $35/hr, helper about $25/hr, W2, paid 40 hours/week) grinds floor with a propane 20-inch grinder and vacuum, rolls polyurea base, broadcasts flake, scrapes, applies polyaspartic top coat in a ~10-hour day. Mike does about 1-2 hours/day oversight; brother Luke does phone sales and in-person quotes; two partners are the field experts. Second crew and Des Moines expansion planned.
unit_economics_claims: Materials about $2.06/sq ft (stated as $1.56 base/flake/top plus ~$0.50 misc); overhead about $1/sq ft; labour about $0.80/sq ft; total about $3.90/sq ft versus $8 price
April revenue $60K, May about $69K, profit over 50%
Cost per lead $30 (best ad) to $100; about 20% close rate
One job can yield $3-4K profit in a day
ideas.startup_cost: About $22-25K as done (including $10K used U-Haul box truck, ~$1K logo, grinder, vacuum); can trim to $15-20K with electric grinder; under $1,000 theoretically by renting a grinder (~$300/day, ~$1K/week) and doing one job.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: First test job in February 2026 (own garage), three paid early-bird jobs within weeks; paid advertising began March; fully booked from April.

acquisition.how: Meta ad creative copy and budget tuning are done with Claude and can be agent-managed, though video content of real jobs and a human calling leads at once are needed.

onboarding.how: Instant phone call to lead, in-person measuring/quoting and deposit; mostly human salesperson.

delivery.how: Physical grinding, coating and flaking by a two-person crew.

billing.how: 10% deposit then payment on completion via card/Venmo/cheque; invoicing and payment links are easily automated.

support.how: Warranty failures and redo jobs require crews on site; customer questions handled by phone.

uk_applicability.notes: Resin flooring exists in the UK but garages are smaller and less common as a status upgrade, so ticket sizes and demand will be lower, and prices would be in GBP per m2. UK weather and damp slabs matter. No contractor licence needed in general, but insurance applies. Meta lead ads and Google LSA-style channels work; GDPR/PECR needs care for calling leads who opted in (acceptable with consent).

risks: Failed floor from wrong product required a full regrind and redo
Physical, weather and humidity dependent; scheduling slips
Low barriers may attract competition drawn by visual ads
Quality and prep variability per garage; reliable crew hiring
Claims are very recent (2-3 months of data)

tactics.name: Instant callback on every lead
steps: Dedicated sales phone to a salesperson
Call every lead within minutes; overnight leads first thing in the morning
Offer to visit same day or afternoon
Take 10% non-refundable deposit to book

quote.text: If somebody submits a lead on our if they click on our ad, we just call them and they're always like, "Wow, you called me right away."
quote.speaker: Mike

tactics.name: Publish pricing in ads (They Ask You Answer)
steps: Put the price per sq ft in the ad and make 'how much does it cost?' the hook
Quote the price at the start of calls to filter tyre-kickers
Pre-qualify distant leads: '$8/sq ft, 500 ft is $4,000, is that within expectations?'

quote.text: People want to know the cost of what you're selling them.
quote.speaker: Mike

tactics.name: Add a qualifying question to Meta lead forms
steps: Replace one-tap instant form with a form asking 'what are you interested in' (interior, garage, exterior, other)
Confirm contact info then submit
Accept higher cost per lead for better intent; redirect to website after submit

quote.text: that one question has like made our quality of leads so much better.
quote.speaker: Mike

tactics.name: Reverse-engineer price from cost
steps: Calculate materials per sq ft
Add monthly overhead divided by target monthly sq ft (7,000)
Add labour at about $35/hr lead plus helper
Double the total to get about 50% gross profit

quote.text: So then that's where I say just double it.
quote.speaker: Mike

tactics.name: Use Claude to run Meta ads
steps: Tell Claude your business, location and audience
Ask for headlines and descriptions for each video
Screenshot Meta Ads Manager and ask Claude how to reallocate budget
Use real process videos, not still images

quote.text: All of our ads are copy and pasted from Claud.
quote.speaker: Mike

tactics.name: Validate with early-bird discount jobs
steps: Do your own garage first as a test
Offer early-bird discount to friends/church for 3 jobs
Learn from failures then launch paid ads

warnings.warning: Using a supplier-suggested product they didn't know caused an early floor failure (bubbling and peeling) and a full regrind and redo.

quote.text: So, we tried using this one product and the floor failed really.
quote.speaker: Mike

warnings.warning: Instant lead forms produced low-intent leads who did not recall submitting; add friction.

quote.text: people were like, you know, cussing us out. Yeah. Who are you? I never clicked anything.
quote.speaker: Mike

warnings.warning: Partnering with strangers is risky; Mike says he got lucky and wouldn't recommend it generally.

quote.text: I don't know that I would like recommend partnering with somebody just because like you said, you never know what you're going to get
quote.speaker: Mike

warnings.warning: Rushing without education makes mistakes costly (wasted materials and time to redo).
Some US states (e.g. California) require contractor licences with prior experience.

quote.text: depending on your state, like California, you can't just like start this up because you got to have experience before you get your contractor license.
quote.speaker: Mike

warnings.warning: Visually appealing ads invite more competitors.

lessons.lesson: The bar in blue-collar services is low: answering the phone, showing up on time and being honest about price differentiates you.

quote.text: the bar is actually low. Yeah. It's Oh, it's so low.
quote.speaker: Mike

lessons.lesson: Charging a premium (not matching the cheapest competitor) attracts better customers, avoids volume grind and holds up in recessions.

quote.text: If you're charging more, then you're naturally serving a higherend clientele.
quote.speaker: Mike

lessons.lesson: Visually satisfying processes make cheap, high-performing social video ads; lead-gen on Meta can beat Google for discretionary visual services.
A cheap, low-risk test (own garage, friends at discount, rented equipment) validates the business before heavy investment.
Reverse-engineer price from full cost (materials, overhead per unit, labour) and double for about 50% gross margin.
Using AI instead of an agency for ads saves thousands per month; paste dashboards into the model for optimization.

quote.text: I'm like, why would we hire an agency if they're just going to do the same thing that I'm doing?
quote.speaker: Mike

lessons.lesson: Choosing materials that shorten the job (one day vs two) is a business decision that raises throughput.
Don't over-plan; start, learn by doing and treat early failures as tuition.

quote.text: I'm like, dude, this is tuition. This is our tuition.
quote.speaker: Mike

lessons.lesson: Fixed capacity means you can hold your price: if a lead balks, another buyer will fill the slot.
A skilled-trade background gives a sales and execution edge but isn't required; partners with field experience de-risked the launch.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with fairly specific cost build-up and consistent numbers, but the business is only about 3 months old, figures are self-reported and unverified, and monthly sales are partly dependent on a few large jobs.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Koerner promotes his TKO Owners community and sponsor GoHighLevel (ad read ignored as an idea).
